page: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a GPU-accelerated server powered by an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at 3.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 56.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with a 400 GB local SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, running on the KVM hypervisor.

The defining feature of this instance is its dual NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs from the Turing family, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. In benchmark testing, this hardware configuration demonstrates top-tier performance in machine learning workloads, achieving top-10% results in LLM inference speeds for both prompt processing and text generation using small (135M) and medium (7B) models. For larger 70B models, prompt processing performance falls into the average tier.

General compute benchmarks, including Geekbench and Passmark CPU tests, place the Intel Xeon processor in the average tier for both single-core and multi-core operations. While memory read bandwidth is average, Passmark memory scores are strong, placing in the top 25%. However, large-block memory write speeds and single-threaded gzip compression are relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware.

Given its hardware profile, the rtx5000-56 offers a specialized resource density that balances dedicated CPU cores with dual GPUs. This makes it highly suitable for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, image processing, ray tracing, and data science tasks. It is less optimal for heavy write-intensive memory operations or purely CPU-bound sequential processing.
